$comment: The 36 follow-up chains (7.6), 12 per office. Assembled by content-assemble from batches chains-mayor, chains-governor, chains-president; seams fixed against the set-ups.

afterSign.text: A study, please: since the band came, 3 fish in 4 nod along.
afterSign.subject: harbours

clippings.sign: GOVERNOR FUNDS STUDY OF FISH IN FOUR-FOUR TIME
clippings.refuse: STUDY SHELVED; FISH STILL NODDING ALONG

afterRefuse.text: The band wrote you a piece: 'Further Study'. Mostly rests.
afterRefuse.subject: bandstands

clippings.sign: GOVERNOR APPLAUDS DURING THE RESTS
clippings.refuse: 'FURTHER STUDY' PLAYED TO AN EMPTY CHAIR

afterSign.text: The band asks for a loud Monday, to balance your silent Sunday.
afterSign.subject: ceremonies

clippings.sign: GOVERNOR SPENDS LOUD MONDAY IN A CUPBOARD
clippings.refuse: LOUD MONDAY MOVED TO A QUIETER DATE

afterRefuse.text: Then sit by the canal with us and say nothing. Rodney is worried.
afterRefuse.subject: ceremonies

clippings.sign: GOVERNOR SILENT FOR AN HOUR; AIDES CONCERNED
clippings.refuse: ANGLERS SIT IN SILENCE, AS USUAL, WITHOUT GOVERNOR

afterSign.text: The bench drifted two locks, to where growers water. Anchor it?
afterSign.subject: inventions

clippings.sign: GOVERNOR'S ANCHOR HOLDS BENCH IN THE WRONG PLACE
clippings.refuse: FLOATING BENCH CONTINUES ITS TOUR OF THE PROVINCE

afterRefuse.text: Then we survey the fish on where to sit. The band hushes for replies.
afterRefuse.subject: inventions

clippings.sign: FISH SURVEYED ON SEATING; NO REPLIES YET
clippings.refuse: FISH NOT CONSULTED; ANGLERS SIT WHERE THEY SAT

afterSign.text: Rodney proposes pressing your one bar as a record. Both sides.
afterSign.subject: vanity

clippings.sign: GOVERNOR'S ONE BAR RELEASED; REVIEWS BRIEF
clippings.refuse: ONE BAR REMAINS ONE BAR

afterRefuse.text: The band kept your bar. Conduct half of it? Less to go wrong.
afterRefuse.subject: bandstands

clippings.sign: GOVERNOR CONDUCTS HALF A BAR; BAND FINISHES IT
clippings.refuse: BAR STILL UNCONDUCTED; BAND PLAYS IT ANYWAY

afterSign.text: Our tuba thrives alone. Each cornet now wants a shelter, by the canal.
afterSign.subject: bandstands

clippings.sign: GOVERNOR CUTS RIBBON ON SHELTER FOR ONE CORNET
clippings.refuse: CORNETS SHARE A SHELTER; NOBODY SPEAKS

afterRefuse.text: Our tuba asks for shop doorways instead. It rattles only 1 pane in 3.
afterRefuse.subject: bandstands

clippings.sign: TUBA IN THE DOORWAYS; WINDOWS ON EDGE
clippings.refuse: TUBA PRACTISES AT HOME; HOME RATTLES

afterSign.text: Open the notebook's shelter, standing just behind the notebook.
afterSign.subject: buses

clippings.sign: GOVERNOR UPSTAGED BY NOTEBOOK AT OPENING
clippings.refuse: NOTEBOOK OPENS OWN SHELTER; SPEECH BRIEF

afterRefuse.text: Then we will pay to name the shops' bench after the founder's pencil.
afterRefuse.subject: buses

clippings.sign: BENCH NAMED AFTER PENCIL; GOVERNOR SITS ON IT
clippings.refuse: PENCIL GOES UNHONOURED; SOCIETY SHARPENS IT

afterSign.text: Till's Teas would pay to put THE GOVERNOR SIPPED HERE at bus stops.
afterSign.subject: signage

clippings.sign: GOVERNOR'S SIP NOW AT EVERY STOP; BUSES MISSED
clippings.refuse: SIP PHOTOGRAPH KEPT IN THE TEA ROOM, BY THE SUGAR

afterRefuse.text: Then pose at our window, admiring the tea. Strictly no sipping.
afterRefuse.subject: portraits

clippings.sign: GOVERNOR ADMIRES TEA THROUGH GLASS; TEA GOES COLD
clippings.refuse: TEA ROOM OPENS WITHOUT GOVERNOR; TEA SERVED ANYWAY

afterSign.text: Enter the pumpkin's glasshouse as a shop window? It is mostly window.
afterSign.subject: vegetable-shows

clippings.sign: GOVERNOR JUDGES SHOP WINDOWS; PICKS A PUMPKIN
clippings.refuse: PUMPKIN WATCHES WINDOW PRIZE FROM ITS GLASSHOUSE

afterRefuse.text: The pumpkin now lives under a cake cover from the shops. Unveil it?
afterRefuse.subject: vegetable-shows

clippings.sign: GOVERNOR LIFTS COVER; PUMPKIN SAYS NOTHING
clippings.refuse: PUMPKIN STAYS UNDER COVER; CAKE LEFT UNCOVERED

afterSign.text: May the show's scales stay on the towpath? They have settled in.
afterSign.subject: vegetable-shows

clippings.sign: SCALES STAY ON TOWPATH; FLOATS NOW WEIGHED BEFORE USE
clippings.refuse: SCALES LEAVE TOWPATH; TOWPATH LIGHTER

afterRefuse.text: A committee to find a second towpath. It has found the first one 6 times.
afterRefuse.subject: vegetable-shows

clippings.sign: COMMITTEE STILL SEARCHING FOR A SECOND TOWPATH
clippings.refuse: SEARCH CALLED OFF; ONE TOWPATH DEEMED PLENTY

afterSign.text: Buses at the bandstand stop wait for each tune to end. Slower tunes?
afterSign.subject: buses

clippings.sign: BAND SLOWS DOWN; THE 7:15 NOW LEAVES AT 7:40
clippings.refuse: BAND KEEPS TEMPO; BUS LEAVES MID-CHORUS

afterRefuse.text: No stop, then. A bench by the bandstand for spotters? Facing the road.
afterRefuse.subject: buses

clippings.sign: GOVERNOR OPENS BENCH; BAND PLAYS TO ITS BACK
clippings.refuse: SPOTTERS STAND TO WATCH BUSES NOT STOP

afterSign.text: Rodney proposes a float with your face, marked STILL AFLOAT.
afterSign.subject: vanity

clippings.sign: GOVERNOR'S FACE FLOAT LAUNCHED; FISH UNIMPRESSED
clippings.refuse: GOVERNOR'S FACE FLOAT FILED FOR FURTHER STUDY

afterRefuse.text: Not holding the float? Then name it, for the Evening Fuss. Something calm.
afterRefuse.subject: ceremonies

clippings.sign: GOVERNOR NAMES FLOAT AFTER SELF; FLOAT BOBS
clippings.refuse: FLOAT PHOTOGRAPHED ALONE; LOOKS DIGNIFIED

afterSign.text: The band will pay to list its tuning up too. It runs all evening.
afterSign.subject: bandstands

clippings.sign: GOVERNOR ATTENDS TUNING UP; LEAVES BEFORE THE MUSIC
clippings.refuse: TUNING UP REMAINS PRIVATE; PRACTICE STILL PUBLIC

afterRefuse.text: Practice is not an event, then. Cut a ribbon, so that it is?
afterRefuse.subject: ribbons

clippings.sign: GOVERNOR CUTS RIBBON ON BAND PRACTICE; BAND STOPS TO WATCH
clippings.refuse: PRACTICE GOES AHEAD UNOPENED

afterSign.text: About the basket: the goose at the bottom was not fruit. It would like an office.
afterSign.subject: geese

clippings.sign: GOOSE GIVEN OFFICE; MAYOR GIVEN GOOSE
clippings.refuse: GOOSE RETURNED TO SENDER, WHO DENIES OWNING A GOOSE

afterRefuse.text: No hard feelings. Please accept this smaller basket. It is one grape.
afterRefuse.subject: ribbons

clippings.sign: MAYOR ACCEPTS GRAPE
clippings.refuse: MAYOR REFUSES GRAPE. GRAPE DEVASTATED

afterSign.text: The pumpkin, now a Freeman of the town, wishes to address the council. It has slides.
afterSign.subject: vegetable-shows

clippings.sign: PUMPKIN'S SPEECH CANCELLED; SLIDES LOST
clippings.refuse: PUMPKIN ADDRESSES EMPTY HALL

afterRefuse.text: The pumpkin has not left its crate since your refusal. It faces the wall.
afterRefuse.subject: vegetable-shows

clippings.sign: MAYOR APOLOGISES TO PUMPKIN
clippings.refuse: PUMPKIN: NO COMMENT

afterSign.text: The museum keeps each ticket it sells. It asks for a shop window.
afterSign.subject: buses

clippings.sign: MAYOR OPENS MUSEUM ANNEXE; IS ASKED FOR A TICKET
clippings.refuse: TICKET MUSEUM FULL. VISITOR ASKED TO WAIT OUTSIDE

afterRefuse.text: No museum? Then a study of each ticket, read aloud in the street.
afterRefuse.subject: committees

clippings.sign: TICKET STUDY READ ALOUD; MAYOR'S TICKET IS A RECEIPT
clippings.refuse: TICKETS STAY IN BOXES, BY DATE. MERVYN READS THEM QUIETLY

afterSign.text: Your name in lights on the 7:02, Mayor. Still late, but brightly.
afterSign.subject: buses

clippings.sign: MAYOR'S NAME IN LIGHTS ON 7:02; SEEN ARRIVING LATE FROM AFAR
clippings.refuse: 7:02 STILL NAMED AFTER MAYOR, STILL LATE, STILL WAVING

afterRefuse.text: The 7:02 kept its name and runs on time. Wave it off? It will not wait.
afterRefuse.subject: buses

clippings.sign: MAYOR WAVES OFF 7:02; 7:02 LATE FOR FIRST TIME IN WEEKS
clippings.refuse: 7:02 ON TIME AGAIN. NOBODY WAVES

afterSign.text: 38 chimes a day, all for buses. The Guild asks for one at opening.
afterSign.subject: clocks

clippings.sign: MAYOR ATTENDS SHOP OPENING CHIME; IT WAS A BUS
clippings.refuse: CLOCK STAYS WITH BUSES; SHOPS OPEN WITHOUT A CHIME

afterRefuse.text: Denied its bus chimes, the clock sulks. Have a word with it?
afterRefuse.subject: clocks

clippings.sign: MAYOR SEEN TALKING TO CLOCK; CLOCK SAYS NOTHING
clippings.refuse: CLOCK STILL SULKING. SPOTTERS TIME IT

afterSign.text: A window of you, judging windows, Mayor. Card: JUDGE'S CHOICE.
afterSign.subject: vanity

clippings.sign: MAYOR'S WINDOW WINS PRIZE; MAYOR WAS THE JUDGE
clippings.refuse: MAYOR DECLINES OWN WINDOW. GLASS RELIEVED

afterRefuse.text: No judge, so all won. A study will pick a winner by how long people look.
afterRefuse.subject: committees

clippings.sign: STUDY PICKS WINNING WINDOW; MAYOR LOOKED LONGEST
clippings.refuse: EVERY WINDOW WINS. NONE OF THEM CHEERS

afterSign.text: The 8:15 left wearing eleven metres of bunting. May it keep it?
afterSign.subject: ceremonies

clippings.sign: BUS LEAVES IN BUNTING; MAYOR WAVES, BUS DOES NOT STOP
clippings.refuse: BUNTING HANDED BACK TO GUILD, FOLDED AND NUMBERED

afterRefuse.text: No bunting, so we hung a single ribbon. Cut it level, Mayor.
afterRefuse.subject: ribbons

clippings.sign: MAYOR CUTS GUILD RIBBON, KEEPS BOTH ENDS
clippings.refuse: RIBBON UNCUT. SHOPPERS STEP OVER IT POLITELY

afterSign.text: Your signpost points both ways, to the shops. We ask for one arm.
afterSign.subject: signage

clippings.sign: MAYOR FOLLOWS OWN SIGNPOST, ENDS UP AT BUS STATION
clippings.refuse: SIGNPOST STAYS FAIR: BOTH ARMS STILL POINT AT SHOPS

afterRefuse.text: The old signpost still points to buses. A study will follow it.
afterRefuse.subject: signage

clippings.sign: SIGNPOST STUDY TAKES WRONG TURN; MAYOR ASKED THE WAY
clippings.refuse: OLD SIGNPOST STILL POINTS AT BUSES; SHOPS FIND OWN WAY

afterSign.text: Your turnip came second, Mayor. A portrait, cropped to leave out the winner?
afterSign.subject: portraits

clippings.sign: TURNIP PORTRAIT UNVEILED; MAYOR STANDS BESIDE IT FOR SCALE
clippings.refuse: SECOND-PLACE TURNIP RETURNS TO PRIVATE LIFE

afterRefuse.text: You would not lend the turnip your name. Till's Teas will pay to lend theirs.
afterRefuse.subject: vegetable-shows

clippings.sign: TILL'S TEAS TURNIP COMES SECOND; MAYOR'S NAME NOT MENTIONED
clippings.refuse: TURNIP STAYS NAMELESS. MAYOR'S NAME STILL ON OFFER

afterSign.text: Your scarecrow is photographed more than you. Pose with it, once?
afterSign.subject: vanity

clippings.sign: MAYOR POSES WITH SCARECROW; CAPTION GETS THEM BACKWARDS
clippings.refuse: SCARECROW STANDS ALONE. CROWS STILL UNCONVINCED

afterRefuse.text: No scarecrow? Then a sign: CROWS BY APPOINTMENT ONLY.
afterRefuse.subject: signage

clippings.sign: CROWS MAKE APPOINTMENT; MAYOR'S DIARY FULL
clippings.refuse: CROWS ATTEND WEIGH-IN WITHOUT APPOINTMENT

afterSign.text: We will pay to book the forecourt yearly. Crowds up 60 %, waiting for buses.
afterSign.subject: vegetable-shows

clippings.sign: MAYOR'S HAT WEIGHED BY MISTAKE; OUTWEIGHED BY A BUS
clippings.refuse: BUSES GET FORECOURT BACK; ONE PUMPKIN LEFT BEHIND

afterRefuse.text: You kept the forecourt for buses. Sign our notebook as a friend of the 8:15?
afterRefuse.subject: buses

clippings.sign: MAYOR SIGNS BUS NOTEBOOK; IS LOGGED AS LATE
clippings.refuse: NOTEBOOK ENTRY UNSIGNED. SPOTTERS NOTE THAT TOO

afterSign.text: The hats had the bandstand a day. They ask for a week, and a hat for it.
afterSign.subject: hats

clippings.sign: HATS KEEP BANDSTAND; MAYOR TRIES ONE ON, KEEPS IT
clippings.refuse: HATS LEAVE BANDSTAND; PUMPKINS TAKE THE STAGE

afterRefuse.text: The pumpkin show kept its stage. Judge it, Mayor, in a hat?
afterRefuse.subject: vegetable-shows

clippings.sign: MAYOR'S HAT JUDGED BEST IN SHOW, BY MAYOR
clippings.refuse: PUMPKIN SHOW GOES AHEAD. NO HATS, ONE ROSETTE

afterSign.text: The hill works. Now a second hill, to admire the first one from.
afterSign.subject: kites

clippings.sign: PRESIDENT BUILDS HILL TO LOOK AT HILL
clippings.refuse: KITES ADMIRE HILL FROM THE CHAIR

afterRefuse.text: Then lend the League the Committee's stepladder. Sundays. Mostly Sundays.
afterRefuse.subject: kites

clippings.sign: HEDGES GO UNTRIMMED ON SUNDAYS, AND MOST TUESDAYS
clippings.refuse: LEAGUE LAUNCHES FROM CHAIR, WITH DIGNITY

afterSign.text: The hedge of you must now match each new haircut. Weekly, I suggest.
afterSign.subject: vanity

clippings.sign: PRESIDENT'S HEDGE HAS BETTER HAIRCUT THAN PRESIDENT
clippings.refuse: HEDGE OF PRESIDENT GROWS OUT; LIKENESS FADES

afterRefuse.text: Your hedge entered the show alone. Come and watch it come second.
afterRefuse.subject: hedges

clippings.sign: PRESIDENT APPLAUDS OWN HEDGE; HEDGE BOWS
clippings.refuse: HEDGE OF PRESIDENT COLLECTS SECOND PRIZE ALONE

afterSign.text: The maze is 99 % free of kites. Fund a search for the rest?
afterSign.subject: kites

clippings.sign: SEARCH PARTY FINDS KITE; SEARCH PARTY NOW LOST
clippings.refuse: LOST KITE GIVEN POSTAL ADDRESS; STAYS LOST

afterRefuse.text: Then a study of the strings in the maze. It meets at the centre, once found.
afterRefuse.subject: hedges

clippings.sign: STRING STUDY GOES IN AT NOON; NOT YET OUT
clippings.refuse: KITE STRINGS STAY IN THE HEDGES, UNCOUNTED

afterSign.text: The band would like to hire one breeze back. For its flags.
afterSign.subject: bandstands

clippings.sign: PRESIDENT SELLS SAME BREEZE TWICE; BREEZE UNAWARE
clippings.refuse: BAND'S FLAGS HANG STILL; CONCERT CALLED 'RESPECTFUL'

afterRefuse.text: Then fund a study of the breeze over Brassby. By kite, of course.
afterRefuse.subject: kites

clippings.sign: WIND STUDY FLIES ALL AFTERNOON; NO FINDINGS LAND
clippings.refuse: WIND OVER BRASSBY STAYS UNMEASURED, AND UNHIRED

afterSign.text: Your first kite is still up, in a hedge. List it as a landmark?
afterSign.subject: kites

clippings.sign: PRESIDENT'S KITE LISTED; HEDGE LISTED WITH IT
clippings.refuse: PRESIDENT'S KITE COMES DOWN ON ITS OWN, AT LAST

afterRefuse.text: No first kite, so no second. The League waits. Let go now?
afterRefuse.subject: kites

clippings.sign: SEASON OPENS LATE; PRESIDENT LETS GO EARLY
clippings.refuse: KITE SEASON STILL WAITING TO START

afterSign.text: The hedge clock says spring. The calendar does not. An inquiry?
afterSign.subject: clocks

clippings.sign: INQUIRY BACKS HEDGE; CALENDAR TO BE TRIMMED
clippings.refuse: HEDGE AND CALENDAR NO LONGER SPEAKING

afterRefuse.text: No clock, then. Stand by the hedge at noon and point up? Once.
afterRefuse.subject: clocks

clippings.sign: PRESIDENT STANDS IN FOR CLOCK; RUNS AN HOUR SLOW
clippings.refuse: HEDGE STILL DOES NOT TELL THE TIME. NEVER DID

afterSign.text: The step we now sit on is 60 % sea. The top step, please.
afterSign.subject: harbours

clippings.sign: BAND MOVES DOWN TO BOTTOM STEP; TUBA GETS WET
clippings.refuse: ANGLERS STAY ON WET STEP. 'QUIETER,' SAYS ONE

afterRefuse.text: Not on the steps, then. Beside them, from a boat. Fund the boat?
afterRefuse.subject: harbours

clippings.sign: BAND PLAYS FROM BOAT; BOAT DRIFTS TOWARDS ANGLERS
clippings.refuse: BAND PLAYS ON QUAY, WAVING AT A BOAT IT LACKS

afterSign.text: A sign for the dim lighthouse: PRESIDENT AT WORK. Lit all night.
afterSign.subject: vanity

clippings.sign: LIGHTHOUSE SAYS PRESIDENT AT WORK; FISH AWAKE TO CHECK
clippings.refuse: FISH SLEEP ON; PRESIDENT'S WORK GOES UNLIT

afterRefuse.text: Then come and say 'hush' to the lighthouse. It may listen to you.
afterRefuse.subject: harbours

clippings.sign: PRESIDENT SHUSHES LIGHTHOUSE; LIGHTHOUSE CARRIES ON
clippings.refuse: LIGHTHOUSE NOT SHUSHED. ANGLERS SHUSH EACH OTHER

afterSign.text: Log one coach from the bench. We will tell you which are coaches.
afterSign.subject: buses

clippings.sign: PRESIDENT LOGS VAN AS COACH; SOCIETY POLITE
clippings.refuse: BENCH LOGS COACHES ALL DAY WITHOUT PRESIDENT

afterRefuse.text: No bench, then. May we lean on the hedge? We have a rota.
afterRefuse.subject: buses

clippings.sign: HEDGE LEANED ON IN SHIFTS; HEDGE NOW LEANS TOO
clippings.refuse: SPOTTERS STAND UNAIDED, LOGGING BRAVELY

afterSign.text: Under the tea lamps, 94 % of coaches are logged 'beige'. One plain lamp?
afterSign.subject: buses

clippings.sign: ONE PLAIN LAMP LIT; TILL'S TEAS CALLS IT 'WEAK'
clippings.refuse: COACH OF THE YEAR: 'BEIGE', AGAIN

afterRefuse.text: Then Till's Teas will hire just the bus stop lamp. It would say TEA.
afterRefuse.subject: signage

clippings.sign: BUS STOP NOW SAYS TEA; NO TEA ARRIVES
clippings.refuse: LAMP BY BUS STOP CONTINUES TO SAY NOTHING

afterSign.text: The pumpkin tours again. It asks for the spotters' front seat. Then yours.
afterSign.subject: vegetable-shows

clippings.sign: PUMPKIN TAKES FRONT SEAT; PRESIDENT IN ROW TWO
clippings.refuse: SPOTTERS KEEP FRONT SEAT; PUMPKIN TOURS IN THE BOOT

afterRefuse.text: The pumpkin toured without you. It kept your seat. Ride the last stop?
afterRefuse.subject: vegetable-shows

clippings.sign: PRESIDENT RIDES LAST STOP; PUMPKIN WAVES FIRST
clippings.refuse: EMPTY SEAT TOURS NINE PROVINCES; WELL RECEIVED

afterSign.text: Your lawn came third of three. Edge it yourself for the rematch?
afterSign.subject: gardens

clippings.sign: PRESIDENT RE-EDGES OWN LAWN. STILL THIRD
clippings.refuse: LAWN UNEDGED; THIRD PLACE KEPT

afterRefuse.text: Then a study of your lawn edges. From the kite field, then from a kite.
afterRefuse.subject: gardens

clippings.sign: LAWN STUDY GOES UP BY KITE; EDGES 'STRAIGHTER FROM ABOVE'
clippings.refuse: LAWN EDGES STAY UNSTUDIED, AND UNEVEN
